statement: The first line holds n; the second holds n integers. Print their sum. One accumulator, one pass: start a total at 0 and add each element as the loop visits it. The shape matters more than the task - the same skeleton counts matches, tracks a maximum or builds a product, with only the update line changing. Use a 64-bit total: the maximum here is a full billion - inside 32 bits but close to the ceiling, and one bigger bound away from wrapping.

example.why: The accumulator walks 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 - one addition per element.

hint: Initialise to 0, add in a loop, print once at the end - resist printing inside the loop.
mistake: Trusting 32 bits out of habit - this problem peaks at a billion and survives, but one larger value bound silently wraps the total.
